questions.stem: Concerning feedback mechanisms in homeostasis, negative feedback:
options: Is the rarest mechanism in the human body
Brings a variable back to its optimal value after a deviation
Amplifies initial changes to accelerate a response
Has no role in homeostasis

questions.stem: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a disease that thickens the alveolar walls. What is the consequence for oxygen diffusion?
options: O₂ diffusion will be increased
O₂ diffusion will be decreased
CO₂ diffusion will also be increased
No effect on gas diffusion

questions.stem: The GLUT-2 transporter carries glucose between blood and cells in both directions, depending on the concentration gradient. What happens in hyperglycemia (raised blood glucose) after a meal?
options: GLUT-2 favors glucose entry into cells
GLUT-2 completely prevents glucose entry into cells
GLUT-2 actively transports glucose against its gradient using ATP
GLUT-2 decreases glucose entry into cells

questions.stem: A patient mistakenly receives an infusion of hypertonic solution instead of an isotonic one. What immediate effect will this have on their red blood cells?
options: They will swell and burst because of massive water entry
They will dehydrate and shrink because water leaves
They will remain unchanged because osmosis only applies to large molecules
They will absorb the hypertonic solution without changing volume

questions.stem: The sodium–glucose cotransporter (SGLT-1) is an example of secondary active transport allowing glucose absorption in the small intestine. What is the principle of this transport?
options: Glucose is transported against its gradient using direct ATP energy
Glucose follows its concentration gradient without needing energy
Glucose is transported with sodium (Na⁺) in the same direction by a symport, using the energy of the sodium gradient
Glucose is exchanged with sodium in opposite directions (antiport)

questions.stem: Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels play a key role in the action potential, passing through three states: open, closed and inactivated. What is their relationship with the falling phase of the action potential?
options: Na⁺ channels stay open to maintain depolarization
Na⁺ channels enter the inactivation phase, preventing further Na⁺ entry
Na⁺ channels reopen to prolong the action potential
Na⁺ channels may be closed and open after a new stimulation

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter is released by postganglionic neurons of the parasympathetic system, and on which receptors does it act?
options: Noradrenaline (NE) acts on alpha and beta receptors
Acetylcholine (ACh) acts on muscarinic receptors
Noradrenaline (NE) acts on nicotinic receptors
Acetylcholine (ACh) acts on adrenergic receptors

questions.stem: G-protein-coupled membrane receptors:
options: Are receptors linked to a G protein composed of three subunits α, β and γ
It is the enzymatic activity of the receptor that activates the G protein
Once the ligand binds its specific receptor, the receptor changes its 3D conformation and activates the G protein
The activated G protein separates from its γ-GTP subunit, which then activates an effector
questions.explanation: It is the α subunit (bound to GTP) that separates and activates the effector.

questions.stem: Receptors:
options: Are only expressed at the cell surface
Have a very weak interaction with their ligand
Bind ligands such as steroid hormones and neurotransmitters
Allow intercellular communication

questions.stem: Intracellular second messengers:
options: Play a role in signal amplification
cAMP is one of these second messengers
Transmit information toward the cytosol
Are made of large molecules

questions.stem: About chemical synapses:
options: Synaptic transmission is unidirectional
The neurotransmitter diffuses from the presynaptic to the postsynaptic element through gap junctions
There is a synaptic delay
The pre- and postsynaptic membranes are continuous

questions.stem: Postsynaptic potentials recorded at neuro-neuronal synapses are phenomena that are:
options: All-or-none
Propagated, always reflecting postsynaptic hyperpolarization
Reflecting conductance changes at the presynaptic level
Gradable and summable

questions.stem: The routes of neurotransmitter elimination are:
options: Reuptake by postsynaptic elements
Diffusion in the synaptic space
Reuptake by presynaptic elements
Enzymatic degradation

questions.stem: The end-plate potential:
options: Is a phenomenon localized at the presynaptic membrane
Reflects a local depolarization of the postsynaptic membrane
Is due to activation of muscarinic-type cholinergic receptors
Statements A, B and C are correct

questions.stem: About the filaments of myofibrils:
options: TnT binds to actin
TnI binds to myosin
Tropomyosin masks the active sites of actin
Myosin binds to TnC
questions.explanation: TnT binds tropomyosin and TnI binds actin.

questions.stem: During muscle contraction:
options: The A bands shorten
The H zones disappear
The Z discs are pulled toward the M line
The light zones remain constant

questions.stem: Calcium binding to troponin causes:
options: The opening of sodium channels
A change in the position of tropomyosin
A conformational change of the T tubule
The uncovering of the actin binding sites for myosin

questions.stem: Among these statements, tick the FALSE one:
options: Myosin heads pull the thick filaments toward the center of the sarcomere
ATP hydrolysis allows the myosin heads to pivot
Propagation of the AP along the T tubules releases calcium
Calcium reuptake into the sarcoplasmic reticulum requires energy
questions.explanation: Myosin heads pull the thin (actin) filaments toward the center.

questions.stem: Concerning energy metabolism:
options: Oxidative phosphorylation does not require oxygen
Anaerobic glycolysis is a rapid source of energy
Aerobic respiration occurs during light but prolonged muscular activity
Anaerobic glycolysis yields 36 ATP molecules

questions.stem: Concerning fluid compartments:
options: The main cation of ECF is potassium (K⁺)
The main cation of ICF is calcium (Ca²⁺)
Intracellular fluid contains more proteins than extracellular fluid
The major cation of ECF is sodium (Na⁺)

questions.stem: Concerning Starling's law:
options: Hydrostatic pressure stays stable
Oncotic pressure is variable
It concerns exchanges between plasma and cytoplasm
It concerns exchanges between plasma and interstitial fluid

questions.stem: Plasma oncotic pressure is generated:
options: By the sodium of the extracellular fluid
By plasma proteins
At the level of the interstitial fluid
By extracellular chloride

questions.stem: Which energy expenditures are associated with thermoregulation?
options: Physical activity
Thermolysis
Postprandial thermogenesis
Thermogenesis

questions.stem: What are the main factors determining energy expenditure apart from basal metabolism?
options: Physical activity
Cardiac activity
Thermoregulation
The specific dynamic action of foods (SDA)

questions.stem: What is the principle of indirect calorimetry?
options: Measuring the amount of oxygen inspired and expired
Determining the energy contained in foods by their O₂ consumption and CO₂ production
Analyzing body temperature after food intake
Measuring energy expenditure solely by heart rate

questions.stem: When managing obesity, the energy balance must be:
options: Zero
Positive
Negative
All these statements are false

questions.stem: Concerning dietary lipids, tick the FALSE answer:
options: Omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids (FA) are essential for humans
Trans fatty acids are industrial fatty acids
Red meats are rich in oleic fatty acid
Omega-6 in excess are pro-inflammatory

questions.stem: Macronutrients are represented by all these nutrients except one. Which one?
options: Carbohydrates
Lipids
Proteins
Vitamins
